mainTopic: Seeds that do not sprout and what the seller repays; how much waste a buyer must accept
overview: The ברייתא about seeds that did not sprout ends with רבי יוסי and the reply 'אמרו לו'. The גמרא asks which of these opinions match the dispute of רב and שמואל about following the majority in money matters. It concludes that the match must involve the תנא קמא, since רבי יוסי and 'אמרו לו' both follow a majority and only argue about which one. A new ברייתא asks whether the seller repays only the value of the seeds or also the buyer's planting expenses. רב חסדא says the 'יש אומרים', who require expenses, is רבן שמעון בן גמליאל. A proof from our משנה is rejected, and the גמרא instead brings a ברייתא where רבן שמעון בן גמליאל makes a worker who ruins food pay even for the embarrassment of the host and his guests. A new משנה then sets how much waste or spoiled goods a buyer must accept. The גמרא starts questioning רב קטינא's claim that this means legumes and not dirt, and that challenge continues on the next עמוד.

steps.title: End of the ברייתא: רבי יוסי and the reply to him
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי rules that the seller of flax seeds that did not sprout returns the value of the seeds. The חכמים answer that many people buy flax seed for other uses.
steps.simpleTranslation: He gives him the value of the seeds. They said to him: Many people buy it for other purposes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a ברייתא it began quoting just before this. רבי יוסי says the seller must pay back the seed money, and the חכמים argue with him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי treats flax seed as something bought for planting, so if it does not sprout, the sale was a mistake. The חכמים reply that many buyers use flax seed for other things. So the seller cannot be blamed, and the sale stands.

keyTerms.meaning: The value of the seeds, meaning the purchase price
For other purposes, meaning not for planting

phrases.english: He gives him the value of the seeds.
phrases.notes: This is רבי יוסי speaking about flax seeds that did not sprout. The start of his words came just before this.

phrases.english: They said to him:
Many buy it for other purposes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא quoted at the end of the previous section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוסי: the seller repays the value of the seeds. The חכמים: no repayment, since many buy flax seed for other uses.

steps.title: Which תנאים match the dispute of רב and שמואל?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which opinions in the ברייתא line up with the dispute of רב and שמואל, and first suggests רבי יוסי against 'אמרו לו'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who are the תנאים that argue like this? If you say it is רבי יוסי and 'they said to him'...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks which two opinions in this ברייתא are the same as the argument of רב and שמואל. It tries the obvious pair first, and this sets up the next step, which knocks that idea down.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, the גמרא said that רב and שמואל's dispute about following the majority in money cases is already a dispute among תנאים. Now it wants to know exactly which תנאים. The first guess is רבי יוסי against 'אמרו לו', since they reach opposite rulings.

keyTerms.meaning: Who are the תנאים, meaning which Sages argue this way
If you say: it introduces a suggestion that will be tested

phrases.english: Who are the tannaim?
phrases.notes: Earlier the גמרא said רב and שמואל's argument matches a dispute among תנאים, and now it asks which ones.

phrases.english: If you say Rabbi Yosei and 'they said to him';

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how the ברייתא just quoted matches the dispute of רב and שמואל.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which two opinions in the ברייתא match the dispute of רב and שמואל about following the majority in money matters.

steps.title: Rejected: both of them follow a majority
steps.stepSummary: The pair רבי יוסי and 'אמרו לו' cannot be the match, because both follow the majority. They only disagree about which majority counts.
steps.simpleTranslation: Both of them follow the majority. One Sage follows the majority of people, and one Sage follows the majority of what is planted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the suggestion it just made. רבי יוסי and the חכמים both accept the majority rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The dispute of רב and שמואל is about whether we follow the majority at all in money cases. Here, 'אמרו לו' counts the number of buyers, and most buyers do not plant. רבי יוסי counts the amount of seed sold, and most of the seed is planted. That is an argument about which majority, not about whether to follow one.

keyTerms.meaning: Both of them
They follow the majority
The majority of people, counting buyers
The majority of planting, counting how much seed gets planted

steps.confusionAlert: Don't assume רבי יוסי is the only one using a majority. The חכמים who answer him use a majority too, just a different one.

phrases.english: both of them follow the majority –
one Sage follows the majority of people,
phrases.notes: This is the 'אמרו לו' opinion: most people who buy flax seed don't plant it.

phrases.english: and one Sage follows the majority of planting!
phrases.notes: This is רבי יוסי: going by amount, most of the seed sold does get planted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the suggestion made in step 2.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the suggested pair (רבי יוסי and 'אמרו לו') is rejected; the question still stands.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Both opinions accept the majority rule, so neither can stand for the side that rejects following the majority in money cases.

steps.title: The match must involve the תנא קמא
steps.stepSummary: The matching dispute is either the תנא קמא against רבי יוסי, or the תנא קמא against 'אמרו לו'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is either the first תנא and רבי יוסי, or the first תנא and 'they said to him'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its answer: the opinion that does not follow the majority is the תנא קמא. It can be set against either of the other two opinions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא said the seller is not responsible even for flax seed, without relying on any majority. So he can stand for the view that we do not follow the majority in money matters. Either of the other two opinions, both of which rely on a majority, can be the opposite side.

keyTerms.meaning: The first תנא, the unnamed opening opinion of the ברייתא
Either ... or

steps.whatToRemember: A dispute about WHICH majority to follow is not the same as a dispute about WHETHER to follow the majority. Only the תנא קמא avoids the majority entirely.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אִי תַּנָּא קַמָּא וְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי,
phrases.english: Rather, either the first tanna and Rabbi Yosei,
or the first tanna and 'they said to him.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אִי תַּנָּא קַמָּא וְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a new answer after the first suggestion was rejected.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The matching dispute involves the תנא קמא, who does not follow the majority, set against either רבי יוסי or 'אמרו לו'.

steps.title: What the seller must repay: seeds only, or expenses too
steps.stepSummary: A new ברייתא: the seller repays the value of the seeds but not the planting expenses. Some say he repays the expenses as well.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: What does he give him? The value of the seeds, but not the expenses. And some say: even the expenses.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic by quoting a ברייתא. It asks how much a seller who is responsible for bad seeds has to pay.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In a case where the seller is responsible, the first opinion says he only returns the seed price. The buyer's planting costs, like paying workers, are not covered. The יש אומרים say he must cover those expenses too.

keyTerms.meaning: Expenses, the costs of planting such as hiring workers
Some say: a second opinion

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the limit on how much the seller owes, which matters in any case where the seller is found responsible.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
What does he give him?
The value of the seeds, but not the expenses.
And some say: even the expenses.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new ברייתא about how much the seller owes.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The first opinion: only the seed value is repaid. The יש אומרים: the planting expenses are repaid as well.

steps.title: Who is the 'some say' opinion?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks who the 'יש אומרים' in the ברייתא is, the opinion that requires the seller to repay expenses too.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who is the 'some say' in that ברייתא?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא wants to know which named תנא stands behind the unnamed 'יש אומרים' opinion from the ברייתא. This question sets up the next move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא in Step 5 had two views: only the value of the seeds, or the expenses too. The second view had no name attached, so the גמרא asks who said it.

keyTerms.meaning: Who?
'Some say', an unnamed opinion in a ברייתא

phrases.english: Who is 'some say'?
phrases.notes: That's the opinion in the ברייתא we just saw, the one that makes the seller pay back the planting expenses too.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks who the unnamed second opinion in the ברייתא of Step 5 is.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The identity of the תנא behind 'יש אומרים'.

steps.title: רב חסדא: it is רבן שמעון בן גמליאל
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא identifies the 'יש אומרים' as רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: it is רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא answers that the 'some say' opinion belongs to רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now we have a name. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל would hold that the seller repays even the buyer's expenses. The גמרא will next try to find where רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says this.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It is', used to say whose opinion a teaching follows

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said:
It is Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל הִיא
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The 'יש אומרים' is רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.

steps.title: Which statement of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל? A suggestion from our משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where רבן שמעון בן גמליאל shows this view and suggests our משנה. It then quotes the first clause of the משנה and draws an inference from it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Which statement of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל do we mean? If you say the one in our משנה: 'One who sells produce to his friend, and the buyer planted it and it did not sprout, even flax seed, the seller is not responsible.' This implies that for garden seeds, which are not eaten, he is responsible.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks where we see that רבן שמעון בן גמליאל holds this. It tries out his ruling in our משנה, quoting the first part of the משנה and drawing a quick inference from it. This sets up the challenge that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא says the seller is not responsible even for flax seed, which is only sometimes eaten. From this the גמרא infers that for garden seeds, which nobody eats, the תנא קמא would make the seller responsible. That inference will matter in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: 'If you say', introducing a possibility the גמרא is testing
Financial responsibility, liability
Flax seed, which is only sometimes eaten

phrases.english: Which Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel?
phrases.notes: He means: which statement of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל shows that he holds this view?

phrases.aramaic: אִילֵּימָא רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל דְּמַתְנִיתִין –
phrases.english: If you say the Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel of our Mishnah,
as we learned: one who sells produce to his friend,
and he planted them and they did not sprout,
and even flax seed,
he is not responsible for them.
This implies: garden seeds that are not eaten,
he is responsible for them.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵי רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל? אִילֵּימָא רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל דְּמַתְנִיתִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Looks for the source of רב חסדא's identification and proposes our משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which ruling of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל shows he requires repaying expenses.

steps.title: The first תנא seems to say the same thing
steps.stepSummary: The end of the משנה has רבן שמעון בן גמליאל ruling that the seller is responsible for garden seeds. The inference just made shows the תנא קמא says this too, so what are they arguing about?
steps.simpleTranslation: Look at the end of the משנה: 'רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: for garden seeds that are not eaten, he is responsible.' But the תנא קמא also says this! Only for flax seed is the seller not responsible, which implies that for garden seeds he is responsible!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out a problem. Based on the inference, the תנא קמא and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל seem to say exactly the same thing about garden seeds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two named opinions in a משנה should disagree about something. If both agree that the seller is responsible for garden seeds, the גמרא needs to find some other point where they differ.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Say the end clause', look at the later part of the משנה
Garden seeds, which are not eaten and are bought only for planting
'Also says this', the two views seem identical

steps.confusionAlert: The תנא קמא here is the first opinion in the משנה, not the תנא קמא of the ברייתא discussed earlier.

phrases.english: Say the end of the Mishnah:
Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
garden seeds that are not eaten,
he is responsible for them.
The first Tanna also says this:

phrases.aramaic: זֶרַע פִּשְׁתָּן הוּא דְּאֵינוֹ חַיָּיב בְּאַחְרָיוּתָן,
phrases.english: it is flax seed that he is not responsible for,
which implies that garden seeds that are not eaten,
he is responsible for them!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵימָא סֵיפָא, רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the inference from Step 8 to show that the two opinions in the משנה appear identical.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading of the משנה in which רבן שמעון בן גמליאל and the תנא קמא disagree about garden seeds.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The תנא קמא's ruling implies the seller is responsible for garden seeds, which is exactly what רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says, so there seems to be no dispute.

steps.title: The real dispute is about planting expenses
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא proposes that the two argue about expenses. The תנא קמא holds the seller repays only the value of the seeds, while רבן שמעון בן גמליאל holds he repays the expenses too.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, isn't it that they disagree about expenses? One master holds the seller repays only the value of the seeds, and the other master holds he repays the expenses as well?
steps.whatsHappening: To give the two opinions a real disagreement, the גמרא suggests they argue about how much the seller must pay for garden seeds. This would support רב חסדא's identification.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both agree the seller is responsible for garden seeds, but they disagree about the amount. If רבן שמעון בן גמליאל requires repaying the expenses too, he matches the 'יש אומרים' of the ברייתא, just as רב חסדא said. The question form ('isn't it?') shows the גמרא is still testing this idea.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Rather, isn't it...?', proposing the only remaining explanation
The buyer's expenses for planting
'There is between them', the practical difference between two views
The value of the seeds
'One master holds', introducing each side of a dispute

steps.confusionAlert: The first 'מר' is the תנא קמא of the משנה, who requires only the value of the seeds. The second 'מר' is רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, who requires the expenses too.
steps.whyThisMatters: This would show that רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's ruling in the משנה is the source for the 'יש אומרים' in the ברייתא, which backs up רב חסדא.

phrases.english: Rather, isn't it that expenses are the difference between them?
One master holds: the value of the seed,
and the other master holds: even the expenses?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the problem from Step 9 by finding a real dispute, which supports רב חסדא from Step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines the point of dispute: the two opinions differ on the amount owed, not on whether the seller is responsible.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The תנא קמא and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל appear to say the same thing about garden seeds.
steps.terutzMaskana: They differ about expenses: the תנא קמא requires only the value of the seeds, and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל requires the expenses too, matching the 'יש אומרים'.

steps.title: Maybe the opinions are reversed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the claim that it is רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, and not the תנא קמא, who requires repaying expenses.
steps.simpleTranslation: How do we know? Maybe it is the other way around!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on Step 10. Who says רבן שמעון בן גמליאל is the one who adds expenses? Maybe the תנא קמא adds expenses and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל requires only the value of the seeds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 10 found an argument about expenses, but nothing in the משנה says which side holds which view. So the identification of the יש אומרים with רבן שמעון בן גמליאל is not yet proven.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know? A request for proof
Perhaps
The opposite, reversed

phrases.english: From where [do we know this]?
Perhaps it is the opposite!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the way Step 10 assigned the two views
steps.kashyaTarget: The assignment of the 'expenses' view to רבן שמעון בן גמליאל
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The argument found in Step 10 could just as easily be flipped between the two תנאים.

steps.title: The later תנא always adds
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the later תנא in a משנה comes to add to the ruling, so רבן שמעון בן גמליאל must be the one requiring more.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is not difficult. Every later תנא comes to add something.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends Step 10 with a general rule. When a second תנא speaks after the first, he is adding to the first ruling, not taking away from it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since רבן שמעון בן גמליאל speaks after the תנא קמא, his view should be the stricter one, the one that adds expenses. That keeps the original assignment in place.

keyTerms.meaning: The later תנא, the one quoted second
To add something

steps.whatToRemember: The rule כׇּל תַּנָּא בָּתְרָא לְטַפּוֹיֵי מִילְּתָא קָא אָתֵי says the second speaker in a משנה usually adds to what came before.

phrases.english: This is not difficult;
every later תנא
comes to add something.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא לָא קַשְׁיָא; כׇּל תַּנָּא בָּתְרָא, לְטַפּוֹיֵי מִילְּתָא קָא אָתֵי
steps.terutzResolutionType: General rule about how the order of opinions works
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The views might be reversed, with the תנא קמא adding expenses.
steps.terutzMaskana: The later תנא adds, so רבן שמעון בן גמליאל is the one who requires expenses.

steps.title: Maybe the whole משנה is רבן שמעון בן גמליאל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof from the משנה by reading the whole משנה as רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's view, with words missing, so there is no argument about expenses.
steps.simpleTranslation: But maybe the whole משנה is רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, and words are missing. It should read: If someone sells produce to his friend, the friend plants it, and it does not sprout, even flaxseed, the seller is not responsible. But for garden seeds, which are not eaten, he is responsible. These are the words of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, because he says that only for flaxseed is the seller not responsible, but for garden seeds, which are not eaten, he is responsible.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers another way to read the משנה. In this reading there are not two opinions at all. The end of the משנה just explains whose view the beginning is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the תנא קמא and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל are the same voice, there is no מחלוקת to explain. So we no longer need to say they argue about expenses. The proof from Steps 8 to 10 falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: Words are missing from the משנה
And this is what it teaches
Responsibility for loss
Flaxseed, only sometimes eaten
Garden seeds, used only for planting

steps.confusionAlert: Here the end of the משנה does not argue with the beginning. It only tells us whose view the beginning is.

phrases.aramaic: וְדִלְמָא כּוּלָּהּ רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל הִיא –
phrases.english: But perhaps all of it is רבן שמעון בן גמליאל,
and it is missing words, and this is what it teaches:
One who sells produce to his friend
and he planted them and they did not sprout,
even flaxseed,
he is not responsible for them,
but garden seeds, which are not eaten,
he is responsible for them;
these are the words of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל;
for רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says:

phrases.aramaic: זֶרַע פִּשְׁתָּן הוּא דְּאֵינוֹ חַיָּיב בְּאַחְרָיוּתָן,
phrases.english: it is only flaxseed that he is not responsible for,
but garden seeds, which are not eaten,
he is responsible for them.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְדִלְמָא כּוּלָּהּ רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל הִיא וְחַסּוֹרֵי מְחַסְּרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the whole proof from the משנה, even after Step 12 defended it
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from our משנה that רבן שמעון בן גמליאל requires expenses
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The משנה can be read as one single opinion, so there is no argument about expenses at all.

steps.title: A new source: a ברייתא about workers who ruin food
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a different source for רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, a ברייתא about workers who ruin wheat, flour, or an animal. It first quotes the opening ruling.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is this statement of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, as a ברייתא teaches: If someone brings wheat to be ground, the miller does not wet it, and he turns it into bran or coarse bran; or someone gives flour to a baker and he bakes it into crumbly bread; or someone gives an animal to a butcher and he makes it a נבילה, the worker must pay, because he is like a paid watchman.
steps.whatsHappening: Having dropped the משנה, the גמרא answers Step 8's question with a new source. This step quotes the first part of the ברייתא and sets up רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's words, which come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The opening ruling says a worker who ruins what he was given must pay, because he is like a paid watchman. That is basic payment for the item itself. The proof comes in the next step, when רבן שמעון בן גמליאל adds more.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, a switch to a new approach
Bran or coarse bran, ruined flour
Underbaked bread that crumbles
He made it a נבילה, an animal not slaughtered properly
A paid watchman

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא הָא רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל – דְּתַנְיָא:
phrases.english: Rather, it is this [statement of] רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, as it is taught:
One who brings wheat to be ground,
and he did not wet them,
and he made them into bran or coarse bran;
[or gave] flour to the baker,
and he baked it into crumbly bread;
[or gave] an animal to the butcher, and he made it a נבילה,
he is liable, because he is like a paid watchman.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא הָא רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected proof from the משנה with a ברייתא
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Where does רבן שמעון בן גמליאל show that one pays more than the item's value? (Step 8)
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: In a ברייתא about workers who ruin food they were given to prepare.

steps.title: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל: pay for embarrassment too
steps.stepSummary: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל rules that the worker also pays for the embarrassment of the owner and his guests, and he cites a custom in ירושלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: He gives him payment for his embarrassment and payment for the embarrassment of his guests. And רבן שמעון בן גמליאל also used to say: There was a great custom in ירושלים. If someone handed over a meal to his friend to prepare and the friend ruined it, he gives him payment for his embarrassment and payment for the embarrassment of his guests.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the proof. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל makes the worker pay more than the value of the ruined food. He also pays for the shame of the host and his guests.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Embarrassment is a loss beyond the item itself, just like the expenses of planting. Since רבן שמעון בן גמליאל charges for it here, it fits that he is the יש אומרים who makes the seller repay expenses too.

keyTerms.meaning: Payment for his embarrassment
His guests
A great custom
One who hands over a meal to be prepared
He ruined it

steps.whatToRemember: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל holds that someone who causes a loss can owe more than the item's value, such as payment for embarrassment. That is why he is identified as the יש אומרים who requires the seller to repay expenses.
steps.whyThisMatters: This finally gives a solid source for רב חסדא's identification in Step 7, after the proof from the משנה was rejected.

phrases.english: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says:
He gives him payment for his embarrassment,
and payment for the embarrassment of his guests.

phrases.aramaic: וְכֵן הָיָה רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: And so רבן שמעון בן גמליאל would say:
There was a great custom in ירושלים:
one who hands over a meal to his friend, and he ruins it,

phrases.aramaic: נוֹתֵן לוֹ דְּמֵי בׇשְׁתּוֹ וּדְמֵי בּוֹשֶׁת אוֹרְחָיו.
phrases.english: he gives him payment for his embarrassment and payment for the embarrassment of his guests.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר: נוֹתֵן לוֹ דְּמֵי בוֹשְׁתּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא begun in Step 14 and supplies the actual proof
steps.raayaObject: רב חסדא's claim that the יש אומרים, who requires expenses, is רבן שמעון בן גמליאל
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא in which רבן שמעון בן גמליאל requires payment for embarrassment beyond the value of the ruined food

steps.title: A second ירושלים custom: the cloth over the doorway
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל continues with another ירושלים custom. A cloth hung over the doorway of a feast, and while it was there, guests could come in.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another great custom in ירושלים: a cloth was spread over the doorway. As long as the cloth was spread, guests came in. Once the cloth was taken down, guests no longer came in.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting the ברייתא from the last step. Here רבן שמעון בן גמליאל describes one more ירושלים custom about guests at a feast.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The main point for the סוגיא was already made in step 15: the worker also pays for the owner's embarrassment. This line simply completes the quote. It adds a second custom showing how carefully ירושלים hosts handled their guests.

keyTerms.meaning: A custom, a common practice
A cloth
Spread out
Guests
Was removed, taken away

phrases.english: Another great custom was in Jerusalem:
a cloth was spread over the doorway;
as long as the cloth was spread,
guests would come in.
Once the cloth was removed,
the guests would not come in.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא quoted in steps 14–15.
steps.raayaObject: The view of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, brought as a source in steps 14–15
steps.raayaSupportSource: The rest of the same ברייתא, describing a second Jerusalem custom
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל reports a second ירושלים custom: while a cloth hung over the doorway of a feast, guests could enter; once it was removed, they no longer entered.

steps.title: How much waste or bad goods a buyer must accept
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה rules that a buyer cannot complain about a small, normal amount of waste or spoiled items. It lists the limit for grain, figs, wine barrels, and jugs.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who sells produce to another: the buyer accepts up to a quarter-קב of waste in every סאה. For figs, he accepts ten wormy figs in every hundred. For a cellar of wine, he accepts ten souring barrels in every hundred. For jugs in the שרון, he accepts ten poor-quality jugs in every hundred.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It sets how much waste or spoiled merchandise a buyer must accept without being able to demand money back.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In any large sale, some of the goods will be imperfect. The משנה sets a fixed limit for each kind of product, and up to that limit the buyer cannot complain. For grain the limit is measured by volume. For figs, wine barrels, and jugs it is counted: ten out of a hundred.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה
A quarter (here, a quarter of a קַב)
Waste, unwanted material mixed into the produce
A measure of volume, larger than a קַב
Barrels of wine starting to turn sour
Jugs of poor quality

steps.whyThisMatters: This משנה sets the basic rule that a buyer is expected to accept normal, small defects. Only defects beyond these limits give him grounds to complain.

phrases.english: MISHNA
One who sells produce to his fellow:
this buyer accepts upon himself
a quarter of waste per סאה.
phrases.notes: The 'quarter' means a quarter of a קב, a small amount compared to a whole סאה.

phrases.english: Figs: he accepts upon himself
ten wormy ones per hundred.
A cellar of wine: he accepts upon himself
ten souring barrels per hundred.
Jugs in the Sharon: he accepts upon himself
ten poor-quality jugs per hundred.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the end of the previous sugya.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A buyer must accept a set small amount of waste or defects: a quarter-קב per סאה for grain, and ten per hundred for figs, wine barrels, and jugs from the שרון.

steps.title: רב קטינא: the waste is legumes
steps.stepSummary: רב קטינא explains that the quarter-קב of waste in the משנה refers to legumes mixed into the grain.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב קטינא taught: a quarter-קב of legumes per סאה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens its discussion of the משנה. רב קטינא explains what kind of 'waste' the buyer has to accept.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה used a general word, טִנּוֹפֶת (waste). רב קטינא narrows it to legumes, which are still food even if they are not what the buyer paid for. By naming only legumes, he seems to say the buyer does not have to accept dirt.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion of the משנה
Taught (a teaching from the time of the משנה)
Legumes, such as beans and lentils

phrases.english: GEMARA
Rav Ketina taught:
a quarter of legumes per סאה.
phrases.notes: He is explaining the משנה's word 'waste': it means legumes mixed in with the grain.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains a word in the משנה of step 17.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The quarter-קב of waste a buyer accepts is legumes.

steps.title: Doesn't the buyer also accept some dirt?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether a buyer really accepts no dirt at all. It begins quoting רבה, through רבה בר חייא קטוספאה, about someone who picks a pebble out of another person's grain.
steps.simpleTranslation: And dirt, he does not accept?! But didn't רבה בר חייא קטוספאה say in the name of רבה: one who picks a pebble out of his fellow's threshing floor...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב קטינא, who seemed to say the buyer accepts only legumes and no dirt. This line sets up the challenge; the quote from רבה continues on the next עמוד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If only legumes count, the buyer would never have to accept any dirt. The גמרא is about to bring רבה's ruling about picking a pebble out of someone else's grain. That ruling will apparently show that some dirt is a normal part of grain.

keyTerms.meaning: Dirt, earth mixed into the grain
But didn't [he] say? (opens a challenge)
A pebble, a small stone
A threshing floor, where grain is processed

steps.confusionAlert: The sentence breaks off in the middle. רבה's ruling about the pebble has not been given yet, so the challenge is not complete here. It finishes on the next עמוד.

phrases.english: And dirt, he does not accept?!
But didn't Rabba bar Chiyya Ketosfa'a say
in the name of Rabba:
one who picks out a pebble from his fellow's threshing floor:

steps.triggerLanguage: וְעַפְרוּרִית לָא? וְהָאָמַר רַבָּה בַּר חִיָּיא קְטוֹסְפָאָה מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַבָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges what step 18 implies: that dirt is not included.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב קטינא's teaching that the accepted waste is legumes, which implies the buyer accepts no dirt
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבה's ruling about removing a pebble from another person's grain seems to treat dirt and stones as a normal part of grain. That would contradict the idea that the buyer accepts no dirt.
